content: Telluric acid is a chemical compound with the molecular formula Te(OH)₆. It exists as a white solid composed of octahedral Te(OH)₆ molecules, and this structural arrangement is retained when dissolved in water. The compound can crystallize in two distinct forms: rhombohedral and monoclinic, both of which maintain the octahedral Te(OH)₆ molecular structure. Telluric acid is classified as a weak acid and is dibasic, meaning it can donate two protons. It reacts with strong bases to form tellurate salts. Telluric acid can be synthesized through the oxidation of elemental tellurium or tellurium dioxide using strong oxidizing agents such as hydrogen peroxide, chromium trioxide, or sodium peroxide. When solutions of telluric acid are crystallized at temperatures below 10°C, they yield Te(OH)₆·4H₂O. Telluric acid exhibits oxidizing properties, as evidenced by its electrode potential, although its oxidation reactions proceed at a slow kinetic rate. The anhydrous form of telluric acid is stable in air at temperatures up to 100°C. However, when heated above this temperature, it undergoes dehydration to form polymetatelluric acid, which is a white, hygroscopic powder with an approximate composition of (H₂TeO₄)₁₀. Further heating results in the formation of allotelluric acid, a viscous acidic liquid with an approximate composition of (H₂TeO₄)₃(H₂O)₄, though its exact structure remains unknown. If subjected to strong heating above 300°C, telluric acid decomposes to produce the α-crystalline form of tellurium trioxide (α-TeO₃). Additionally, telluric acid reacts with diazomethane to form the hexamethyl ester, Te(OMe)₆. In most of its compounds, telluric acid and its salts feature tellurium in a hexacoordinate state. For example, magnesium tellurate (MgTeO₄) is isostructural with magnesium molybdate and contains TeO₆ octahedra. Metatelluric acid (H₂TeO₄), which would be the tellurium analogue of sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), has not been observed. Allotelluric acid, with an approximate composition of (H₂TeO₄)₃(H₂O)₄, is poorly characterized and may represent a mixture of Te(OH)₆ and polymeric forms of (H₂TeO₄)n. Tellurous acid (H₂TeO₃) is known, but it is also not well characterized.
